name: Affordability Crisis
title: Say No to Corporate Giveaways and Yes to Affordable Housing in the Railyards
description: Sacramento is proposing a $222 million taxpayer subsidy for wealthy developers in the Railyards, a plan that only has 6% affordable housing. 6% affordable housing is shamelessly inadequate. Sacramento deserves better!   Last year, a clear majority of Railyards residents protested the $92 million EIFD (Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District) subsidy, which forced the termination of the subsidy proposal under California law. Now, a year later, Sacramento is bringing the same bad deal, but with all residents drawn out of the plan boundaries to try to take away ability to reject the proposal. Instead of improving the plan, Sacramento is trying to undemocratically silence residents.    Sacramento must stop putting wealthy developers before everyday residents struggling with housing affordability. The City is facing an affordable housing crisis. The Railyards redevelopment will double the size of downtown Sacramento. If our city leaders really take housing affordability and homelessness seriously, this is their biggest opportunity to set us on a new path.
